turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Alright, let's start. Main thing today is the session store. Arjun, where are we?

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: So right now sessions live in Redis, and we're seeing latency spikes on the Kubernetes cluster, about two hundred milliseconds at the ninety fifth percentile.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: It's only on three nodes, but it's enough to hurt the checkout flow.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Is that a Redis problem or a networking problem?

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: Mostly Redis. The connection pool thrashes under load. I think we should move the session store to PostgreSQL.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: PostgreSQL will be slower per read, but it's far more predictable, and we already run it in staging.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Okay. Let's do it. We're moving the session store from Redis to PostgreSQL. That's decided.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: While we're at it, maybe we should switch the internal calls from REST API to gRPC. It might help the latency too.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Let's park that one. Interesting, but not this sprint, and I don't want to change two things at once.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: Agreed. I'll benchmark the PostgreSQL session store latency and have numbers by Friday.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Good. Sam, can you update the Grafana dashboard so we can actually see the new metrics?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Yes, I'll take the Grafana dashboard.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: And someone needs to document the rollback procedure before we ship anything.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: One more thing. We are not going to do the OAuth migration this sprint. It's blocked on the vendor.
